title: Survivors of Head-On Crashes
statement:
Rocks are lined up on a track, listed from left to right in rocks. The size of each rock is the absolute value of its number, and the sign is its direction: positive moves right, negative moves left. All rocks move at the same speed.

When two rocks meet head on, the smaller one is destroyed. If they are the same size, both are destroyed. Rocks moving in the same direction never meet, and neither do rocks moving apart.

Return the rocks that are left after every crash has happened, in their left-to-right order.

examples.why: The −5 hits the 7 first and loses. The 4 never meets anything.
The −8 destroys the 5, then keeps going and destroys the 3. The 2 moves right, away from it.
−2 moves left with nothing ahead of it. 3 and −3 are equal and both break. Then −1 moves left freely: −2 and −1 move the same way and never meet.

hints: A rock moving left can only hit rocks to its left that move right. Which of those does it hit first?
Process rocks left to right and keep the survivors so far. A new left-moving rock fights the most recent right-moving survivor, and possibly the one before it, and so on.

Use a stack of survivors. While the new rock moves left and the top moves right: pop the top if it is smaller, pop it and drop the new rock if equal, drop the new rock if the top is bigger. Push the new rock if it survives.

explain.intuition:
Only one pattern produces a crash: a right-mover on the left and a left-mover on the right. If you scan from left to right and keep the survivors so far, a new left-moving rock first meets the nearest right-mover to its left, which is the last one you kept. If it wins, it carries on to the next one back. That "most recent first" order is a stack.

A new right-moving rock cannot hit anything already kept, so it is simply pushed. Each rock is pushed once and popped at most once, so the whole thing is linear, even though one rock can wipe out many.
steps: For each rock x: while x < 0 and the top is positive and smaller than -x, pop the top.
If the top is positive and equal to -x, pop it and drop x.
Else if the top is positive and bigger, drop x.
Otherwise push x. The stack, bottom to top, is the answer.
pitfalls: Making [-4, 4] collide. Those rocks move apart.
Stopping after one crash. A big left-mover keeps going, as in [3, 5, -8, 2].
Keeping one of two equal rocks. Equal sizes destroy both.

solutions.title: Repeat until nothing collides
solutions.idea: Find any adjacent pair moving towards each other, resolve that crash, and start over. Simple but quadratic.

solutions.title: Stack of survivors
solutions.idea: A left-mover fights the most recent right-moving survivor first. Keep survivors on a stack and pop the ones it destroys.

followups: Rocks have different speeds. Which crashes happen first now, and does a stack still work?
Return how many crashes each surviving rock was involved in.
